text:
anya: Heads-up — ran a post-CMK rotation restore smoke against staging snapshots and hit a cluster of AccessDenied on decrypt. past rotation completed last night.

tarun: can you paste the restore/log output? which snapshot id?

anya: snapshot: snap-stg-2026-03-20-02

anya: logs:
```
restore-agent: starting restore for snap-stg-2026-03-20-02
kms: Decrypt failed, error=AccessDenied, message=User: arn:aws:sts::123456:assumed-role/backup-agent is not authorized to use CMK arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456:key/abcd-ef01
Restore aborted
```

lisa: :eyes: backup-agent role should still have kms:Decrypt via grant. we rotated CMK policy and added a deny for old-roles — maybe overly broad.

sana: we scoped the deny to prevent old tenant roles from using it. need to check if the backup-agent assumed-role was included in the allow list or got shadowed.

sec-oncall: tagging in the runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/encops/restore-playbook — step 2 checks grants and ephemeral grants.

anya: I ran `aws kms list-grants --key-id abcd-ef01` and saw no active grant for backup-agent.

tarun: do we use grants for short-lived restores or rely on IAM allow? I thought backup process uses a long-lived grant created during snapshot upload.

sana: upload creates a grant with operations [Decrypt, GenerateDataKey], expiration null. rotation process attempts to re-create equivalent grants for the new CMK but there's a race if rotation happened before grant copy job finished.

devops-bot: [automated] rotation-job completed 2026-03-20T01:45:12Z, grant-copy triggered, 3/5 copy workers acknowledged.

anya: looks like 2 failed copy workers timed out and we never retried — explains missing grants on new key.

lisa: quick mitigation: 1) re-create grant for backup-agent principal on current CMK, 2) allow fallback to previous CMK for 24h via key policy tweak, 3) schedule grant-copy retry with heartbeat reporting.

tarun: can someone run the grant creation now? sample command:
```
aws kms create-grant --key-id abcd-ef01 --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::123456:role/backup-agent --operations Decrypt GenerateDataKey
```

sana: i'm on it. will create grant and test restore. also adding a temporary CloudWatch alarm for grant-copy failures.

sec-oncall: note for audit: escalate to SOC if more than 5 tenants fail restore. include KMS grant ops in audit events.

anya: i ran the create-grant command, got GrantId=gr-0a1b2c3d, then retried restore and it progressed past decrypt. restoring full DB now.

anya: restore succeeded for snap-stg-2026-03-20-02. tagging in the runbook that grant-copy needs stronger retry and visibility.

lisa: action items:
- sana: add retry/backoff and a per-copy worker heartbeat + metrics (PR by EOD)
- tarun: update rotation-runbook to include immediate grant audit and recovery steps
- sec-oncall: add KMS grant events to 90-day audit log retention

sana: will open an RFC for a safer rotation: create mirror grants before switching, require 5/5 copy ack, and mark rotation complete only after verification.

tarun: also add an emergency play to temporarily relax key policy to allow previous CMK for 1 hour when grant-copy fails (with guard rails).

anya: thanks — closing this thread once PRs linked. cc @devops-bot please post back when grant-copy metric exists.

devops-bot: [automated] created alarm "kms-grant-copy-failures" threshold=1 over 5m, created dashboard panel.

lisa: nice. filing post-rotation remediation ticket and notifying support to pause customer restores on rotation windows until we have the new checks in place.

anya: filing ticket now: https://issues.redwood.ai/INC-6722 — summary: missing KMS grants after rotation -> restore failures; owners: sana/tarun, ETA 48h.

sec-oncall: good triage. mark as priority-high for encops and infra. :white_check_mark:
